title: A step toward: Petersen graph: some circuit with at most 6 AND gates, ORs free, is correct on its partial function with each variable bare in at… (step 2 of 2)
formal_statement: ∀ (x1 x2 : Fin (6 : ℕ) → ℕ) (x3 : Finset (Fin (6 : ℕ))),   (∀ (x4 : Fin (6 : ℕ)), x1 x4 < (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x4) ∧ x2 x4 < (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x4)) →     have x5 : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit (10 : ℕ) := { size := (6 : ℕ), leftVars := fun (x5 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => {x6 : Fin (10 : ℕ) | (x1 x5).testBit ↑x6 = Bool.true}, leftGates := fun (x5 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => {x6 : Fin (6 : ℕ) | x6 < x5 ∧ (x1 x5).testBit ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x6) = Bool.true}, rightVars := fun (x5 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => {x6 : Fin (10 : ℕ) | (x2 x5).testBit ↑x6 = Bool.true}, rightGates := fun (x5 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => {x6 : Fin (6 : ℕ) | x6 < x5 ∧ (x2 x5).testBit ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x6) = Bool.true}, outVars := ∅, outGates := x3 : PEqualNP.AndCount.AndCountCircuit (10 : ℕ) };     have x6 : ℕ → ℕ := fun (x6 : ℕ) => List.foldl (fun (x7 : ℕ) (x8 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => if x7 &&& x1 x8 ≠ (0 : ℕ) ∧ x7 &&& x2 x8 ≠ (0 : ℕ) then x7 ||| (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x8) else x7) (x6 % (1024 : ℕ)) (List.finRange (6 : ℕ));     ∀ (x7 : ℕ), x5.eval {x8 : Fin (10 : ℕ) | x7.testBit ↑x8 = Bool.true} = Decidable.decide (∃ x8 ∈ x3, (x6 x7).testBit ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x8) = Bool.true)
plain_statement: For any six pairs of numbers (L_i, R_i) with L_i and R_i below 2^(10+i), and any set O of gate indices, take the six-gate AND-count circuit on ten variables whose gate i has as left side the variables v with bit v of L_i set and the earlier gates j < i with bit 10+j of L_i set, the right side likewise from R_i, no output variables, and output gates O. On every input x it outputs exactly what this evaluation gives: put x in bits 0-9; for i = 0 to 5 set bit 10+i when the word so far shares a bit with L_i and with R_i; output whether bit 10+i is set for some i in O.
